document.title: Report unhandled rejections, stop stb_ds seed race, log dropped events
document.summary: The JS thread now reports promise rejections that stay unhandled to the Deck App Failure Screen. Separately, the vendored stb_ds no longer writes its global hash seed, and the event queue logs a warning when it drops an event.
document.why: [An unhandled promise rejection is swallowed](source:s1) because the JS thread never installs QuickJS's rejection tracker. [The JS and main threads both write stb_ds's global hash seed](source:s2), a data race.

sources.title: Unhandled promise rejections in Deck Apps fail silently
sources.gist: Install a rejection tracker; report or log; document the choice; cover with a harness scenario.

sources.title: Data race on stb_ds global hash seed between JS and main threads
sources.gist: Seed stb_ds once at startup and ensure nothing re-seeds later.

sources.label: PR #81
sources.gist: Fixes #69 and #78; host, sanitized, smoke and Vita builds pass in Docker.

lookFor: [#78 asks to call `stbds_rand_seed` once at startup](source:s2); the change instead removes the LCG step in `stbds_make_hash_index`, because that step re-seeds the global on every new map, so a startup call alone would not remove the write.

parts.name: Unhandled rejections
parts.summary: A QuickJS rejection tracker holds unhandled rejections until microtasks drain, then reports the rest as uncaught errors.

parts.name: Hash seed race
parts.summary: stb_ds stops advancing its global seed per new map, and full-queue drops get a warning.

groups.title: Rejection tracker on the JS thread
groups.why: [Unhandled rejections never reach the Failure Screen](source:s1).
groups.summary: `track_rejection` in `js_runtime.c` collects unhandled promises, `drain_microtasks` reports the survivors through the new `js_report_rejection`, which shares `report_value` with `js_report_exception`.
lookFor: Subtle: rejections are judged once per `drain_microtasks`, so a `catch` attached in a later `setTimeout` arrives too late and the Deck App already shows the Failure Screen.
The Failure Screen message is the rejection reason itself (e.g. `Error: boom`); only the log line carries the `[unhandled rejection]` source tag.

groups.title: Harness scenarios
groups.why: [The issue asks for a harness scenario](source:s1).
groups.summary: `js_limits_harness` runs an unhandled rejection at boot, one in a timer, and one whose `catch` attaches in a later microtask, which must leave the app running until a sentinel `nativeReportDeckAppError` fires.

groups.title: stb_ds stops writing its global seed
groups.summary: The vendored `stbds_make_hash_index` copies the global seed into each new table and no longer advances it, so after startup the global is only read.
lookFor: Every hash map now starts with the same seed `0x31415926`; hashing stays consistent because each table already stores its own `t->seed`.

groups.title: Warn on dropped input events
groups.why: Drops on a full queue were silent; the drop-newest policy stays, now with a log line.
groups.summary: `event_queue_push` logs a `TraceLog` warning after unlocking when the queue is full, and `event_queue_harness` now links raylib and silences the log.
lookFor: Every dropped event logs one warning, so a sustained overflow logs once per push.

commits.subject: fix(core): stop stb_ds writing its global hash seed, log dropped events
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
stb_ds advanced a global seed every time any thread created a hash map, a data race between the JS and main threads. Seeding once at startup would not help since every new map re-seeds, so the vendored header now only reads the seed. event_queue_push also logs a warning when it drops an event on a full queue.

Fixes #78

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.subject: fix(runtime): report unhandled promise rejections to the Failure Screen
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Install a QuickJS rejection tracker on the JS thread. Rejections without a handler are held until the microtask queue drains, dropped if a handler attaches in the meantime, and otherwise reported like any other uncaught Deck App error.

Fixes #69

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
